svg.text: E1 · What the validator reads — row timestamps only
Two checks: largest gap ≤ allowed (normal budget = interval + 2·timeout = 5 s); and gaps above the budget sum to
≤ 5 % of the window. Neither sees slots.
measurement window [4 s, 12 s) → 8 expected slots per host
largest node-b row gap = 1.2 s (row timestamps = request midpoints)
node-b answers every request in 1.2 s. Its rows are 1.2 s apart at worst — under the 5 s budget, so it never
enters either sum. Verdict: coverage OK.
node-c's exporter came up at slot 3. Its first row is at 3.1 s; the boundary check only needs one row before the
window start, so it passes too.
Both hosts pass with room to spare. The validator has no number that says how many samples node-b should have
E2 · What the slot grid reads — the same events bucketed onto one global grid, tallied per host
One anchor and one interval for the session (the collector's shared _collector_grid). Slot k starts at the same
instant on every host; each host is then classified per slot: ok / late / missed / unaccounted.
measurement window [4 s, 12 s) → 8 expected slots per host
largest node-b row gap = 1.2 s (row timestamps = request midpoints)
Inside the window every host is expected on all 8 slots. node-a: 8/8 ok. node-c: 8/8 ok — its late start is
outside the window and doesn't count against it.
node-b: 7 rows + 1 missed (sample_schedule_overrun) = 8. Loss = 1/8 = 12% in this window (1 slot in 6 at exactly
1.2×; the live probe on 68fe74ec measured 23 % with real HTTP overhead), with every individual gap still ≤ 1.2
s. This is the number the timestamp checks cannot see.
Grey = unaccounted: slots with no row and no missed range (node-c slots 0–2: the collector never got a
successful poll, so nothing was recorded). Over the whole session that would read as loss; bounded to the window
A cumulative check is (expected − rows) / expected per host over the window, against the same 5 % — cadence-
relative by construction, and independent of which gaps happen to straddle the budget.

g.text: request in flight; row timestamp = midpoint (┃)
request failed / timed out — no row (endpoint_timeout)
unaccounted — no row and no missed range for this (host, slot)
measurement window — the only slots a verdict should count
